chunks: What will God do with your punishment if you are grateful and believe? And God is Responsive to gratitude, Cognisant.

key_terms.شَاكِرًا: Responsive to gratitude / The One who appreciates small deeds

ai.seo_question: Why is there no punishment for believers who are grateful?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse clarifies that divine punishment is not merely a transactional response to disbelief but is contingent upon the absence of faith and gratitude; since God is 'Shakir' (He who appreciates the small acts of worship) and 'Alim' (All-Knowing of the heart's state), He accepts the believers' sincere gratitude and faith, thereby sparing them from the chastisement reserved for those who reject the truth. This highlights the Shia emphasis on the internal state of 'iman' (faith) and 'shukr' (gratitude) as the primary criteria for divine mercy, rather than mere ritualistic observance.
